Just a heads up.

Use terminal to update, Octopi can cause problems.

Use sudo pacman -Syyu to update.

Use sudo pacman-mirrors -g to get faster update times.

If you can't update do this:

login as root using the su

then paste this

pacman-key --init

pacman-key --populate archlinux manjaro

pacman-key --refresh-keys

If the dir manager is giving you a headache login as root using the su and paste this:

dirmngr </dev/null

then repeat the previous steps for refreshing the keys.

That should keep you running Manjaro forever. Also, KDE Plasma 5 is still just a little bit buggy, but not much. Some minor annoyances are to be expected.

As nobody is taking about it yet, I'll weigh in on my near year on Plasma 5.

It's gorgeous. Hands down, no question about it. It's snappy, looks good, works well, hasn't crashed my computer, used too much memory, all the good stuff you want from a wm. That being said, the other KDE applications have only just caught up to being ported to QT 5 and Frameworks 5. I'm not so sure all of them are even there yet, and there seems to have been a decent amount of applications that are just done, though I can't comment on that.

If you've used KDE before, there are the usual oddities, things not working always the way they seem, and the themers haven't caught up yet. It's on a very fast release cycle and my distribution (Gentoo) has not stabilized any part of it yet, but it's always updated in the official overlay.

Overall, I recommend Plasma 5 to everyone who wants a beautiful, functional wm for sure.
